---
title: "Python output"
jupyter: python3
---

Every kind of output a data-analysis course produces, written the ordinary
way. The rule under test: `print()` stays console text; a displayed object
(the cell's last expression, `display(x)`) is rendered according to its type.

## Data frames

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "city": ["Padova", "Venezia", "Verona", "Vicenza", "Treviso"],
    "pop": [210_000, 250_000, 257_000, 111_000, 85_000],
    "area": [92.85, 415.9, 198.9, 80.57, 55.58],
    "delta": [-0.4, 1.2, -2.5, 0.0, np.nan],
})
df
```

The same frame through `print()` stays console text:

```{python}
print(df)
```

Long, wide, and with a hierarchical index:

```{python}
long = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(size=(100, 3)), columns=["a", "b", "c"])
long
```

```{python}
wide = pd.DataFrame(rng.integers(0, 100, size=(4, 20)), columns=[f"col_{i}" for i in range(20)])
wide
```

```{python}
sales = pd.DataFrame({
    "region": ["N", "N", "S", "S", "N", "S"],
    "year": [2024, 2025, 2024, 2025, 2025, 2024],
    "product": ["a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "a"],
    "units": [10, 12, 7, 9, 3, 5],
})
sales.groupby(["region", "year"]).agg(units=("units", "sum"), n=("units", "size"))
```

```{python}
sales.pivot_table(index="region", columns=["year", "product"], values="units", aggfunc="sum")
```

```{python}
ts = pd.DataFrame({"value": rng.normal(size=6)},
                  index=pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=6, freq="MS"))
ts["kind"] = pd.Categorical(["x", "y", "x", "y", "x", "y"])
ts
```

`head()` and `describe()`, the two most common calls:

```{python}
long.head()
```

```{python}
long.describe()
```

A Styler keeps its own formatting:

```{python}
df.style.format({"area": "{:.1f}"}).hide(axis="index")
```

## Series

```{python}
df["pop"]
```

```{python}
sales["product"].value_counts()
```

```{python}
pd.Series(rng.normal(size=50), name="noise")
```

## Arrays

```{python}
A = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
A
```

```{python}
B = rng.normal(size=(4, 4)).round(3)
B
```

```{python}
big = np.arange(10_000).reshape(100, 100)
big
```

```{python}
np.eye(3, dtype=bool)
```

One-dimensional, three-dimensional and non-numeric arrays stay as numpy shows them:

```{python}
np.linspace(0, 1, 5)
```

```{python}
np.arange(24).reshape(2, 3, 4)
```

```{python}
np.array(["a", "b"]), np.array([1 + 2j, 3 - 1j])
```

`print()` of an array is console text:

```{python}
print(A)
```


## Loops and progress lines

```{python}
loss = 1.0
for epoch in range(1, 6):
    loss *= 0.7
    print(f"epoch {epoch}  loss={loss:.4f}  acc: {1 - loss:.3f}")
```

## Messages and errors

```{python}
import warnings
warnings.warn("this is a warning")
print("and this goes to stdout")
```

```{python}
import sys
print("written to stderr", file=sys.stderr)
```

```{python}
1 / 0
```

## Rich objects from other libraries

```{python}
import sympy as sp
x = sp.symbols("x")
sp.integrate(sp.exp(-x**2), (x, -sp.oo, sp.oo)), sp.Matrix([[1, x], [x**2, 0]])
```

```{python}
from IPython.display import Markdown, Math, display
display(Math(r"\int_0^1 x^2\,\mathrm{d}x = \tfrac13"))
Markdown("Some **markdown** from code.")
```

## Plots

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(t, np.sin(t), label="sin")
ax.plot(t, np.cos(t), label="cos")
ax.set_xlabel("t")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
long.plot(kind="hist", alpha=0.6, bins=20);
```

```{python}
import seaborn as sns
sns.boxplot(data=long.melt(), x="variable", y="value");
```
